data.body:
=== HANDOFF #18 ADDENDUM — a CI failure mode worth knowing, and its fix ===

**A change based on an older commit can fail CI on a step whose SCRIPT its tree does not contain — and
it looks nothing like a rebase problem.** 1276 (2b16) took `Verified -1` with:

    python: can't open file '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/check_config_reads.py':
    [Errno 2] No such file or directory
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.

Diagnosis, and the part that misleads: `build-and-test` DID run (so it was NOT the concurrency-group
cancellation trap from #15/#17 — lint + type-check + pip-audit all passed and only the four pytest legs
failed), and there was no failing TEST at all. **CI takes the WORKFLOW from main but the CODE from the
patchset.** `3ad3abe72` ("6754: config-is-read gate for schema fields", change 1257) added
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:434 → python scripts/check_config_reads.py` AND
`scripts/check_config_reads.py` atomically. 1276 was based on `6cdd4b00d9`, which predates it, so the
workflow-from-main invoked a script the patchset tree lacked. Every older-based change in flight hits
this: 1279/1280 were based on `ba3c06ee47` and would have failed identically.

**Fix: REBASE. This is the #17 trap "Rebase-If-Necessary applies at SUBMIT, not to CI" in its most
confusing dress** — the symptom is a missing FILE, so it reads as a broken main rather than a stale base.
All three changes were rebased onto `gerrit/main` and re-pushed; the diff stat was checked against
`gerrit/main` each time to confirm nothing was swept in (4 files / 782 insertions for 1276; 3 files /
750 for the 1279+1280 stack), and `scripts/check_config_reads.py` now runs clean locally.

**A wrong turn I took, recorded so nobody repeats it:** I first checked for the script with
`git cat-file -e <ref>:scripts/check_config_reads.py` inside a `for` loop with `&&`/`||` chaining and got
"MISSING" for EVERY ref including current main — which made it look like main itself was broken for
everyone. That reading was wrong. `git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> -- <path>` gave the correct answer
(present on main, absent on both older bases). **Use `ls-tree` for per-ref file existence**, and be
suspicious of a result that says the whole repo is broken.

**The `Missing tree <sha>` push error from #18 is fixable.** 2b16's agent hit it twice pushing a
rebased tree (including with `--no-thin`) and gave up, pushing from the original base — which is what
caused the CI failure above. Running a FULL `git fetch gerrit` (all refs, not `git fetch gerrit main`)
before the push made it succeed first try: the client then has the remote's objects and builds a valid
thin pack. Do that instead of abandoning the rebase.
